subject: MSA / Order Form — audit rights scope, pen-test staging & evidence rotation
messages:
From: Anita Desai <anita.desai@medicohealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicohealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on audit rights / pen test window for Redwood MSA

Connor —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. As we move toward signature on the Order Form we need to confirm the exact language and operational expectations in the security exhibit. Two quick asks from our InfoSec and procurement teams: 

1) Pen test access: we need to understand the expected notice window, permitted testing windows (staging vs prod), and whether Redwood requires observation or can accept vendor-managed tests.

2) Audit & evidence cadence: we typically ask for SOC 2 report delivery plus a quarterly evidence cadence for a defined set of controls (user provisioning, encryption configs, access logs). We are open to sampling-based evidence but need a clear rotation plan and owner responsibilities.

3) Audit rights scope: do you allow on-site/remote audits, and are there caps on audit frequency or number of auditors?

I attached our questionnaire to make this concrete. Can you and your legal lead propose specific exhibit language or a short playbook we can use to slot into our procurement checklist?

We are aiming to complete legal review by 8/20 so any draft language this week would be helpful.

Regards,
Anita Desai
Sr. InfoSec Manager — MedicoHealth
(attachment: MedicoHealth_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Anita Desai <anita.desai@medicohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T13:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit rights / pen test window for Redwood MSA

Anita —

Thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire — that helps. High-level proposal below; attaching a short draft security exhibit for your review (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_Draft_v1.pdf). We can tighten language with Karthik from legal once you confirm operational expectations.

Proposal (summary):
- Pen test: Redwood accepts third-party pen tests with a 30-day advance notice for production-facing tests; staging tests preferred where feasible and allowed. We require a mutually agreed test plan and two-week blackout windows around major releases; Redwood engineers can observe but do not need to be present for vendor-managed tests.
- Audit rights: Remote evidence review is primary. On-site audits permitted with 30 days' notice and limited to 1 on-site event per 12-month period unless a material incident justifies additional access.
- Evidence cadence: Recommended rotational sampling — quarterly delivery of control artifacts for prioritized control groups; full SOC 2 report annually. Redwood will maintain a 12-month rolling evidence repository and designate an evidence owner for each control grouping.
- Scope alignment: We propose defining the control sets in an appendix (controls A/B/C) and mapping each to an evidence cadence to avoid ad-hoc requests.

If that approach aligns with MedicoHealth's requirements I will loop in Karthik with redline suggestions and propose a short playbook (sequence: notice -> test plan -> evidence request -> closure report).

Next steps: Please confirm whether staging tests are acceptable and whether your procurement team will require DocuSign for the final Order Form or a composite signature flow.

Connor —

Quick clarifications:
- Staging tests: acceptable as long as the environment mirrors production configs for authentication and data handling. If staging cannot be used, we will expect a shorter notice window (we prefer 14 days max for production tests).
- Observation: vendor-managed tests are fine; we do require a remediation window commitment from Redwood of 30 days for medium/high findings and an incident response owner named.
- DocuSign: procurement prefers DocuSign for the Order Form and any exhibit attachments.

I copied Samir from procurement — he will confirm DocuSign flow and whether they need redlined POSA fields on the Order Form.

Thanks,
Anita
(Referenced attachment from our side: MedicoHealth_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Anita Desai <anita.desai@medicohealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit rights / pen test window for Redwood MSA

Anita / Connor —

Appreciate the specifics — I've sketched redlines that try to balance MedicoHealth's risk needs with predictable operational controls for Redwood. Key proposed edits (see attached redline):

1) Pen testing: Add explicit requirement that customer provides a written test plan 15 business days prior to any production test; Redwood will provide a point of contact and confirm blackout dates within 5 business days of receipt. Limit production-facing tests to 2 per 12-month period unless both parties agree otherwise.

2) Notice & scope: For remote evidence requests, define a maximum 10 control artifacts per quarter per control group, with requests to be batched and responded to within 10 business days. This prevents ad-hoc one-off asks.

3) On-site audits: Allow on-site with 30 days' notice, capped at 1 per 12 months. Add standard health/safety and access policies and require auditors to sign an NDA and follow Redwood on-boarding steps.

4) Findings & remediation: Commitment to provide remediation plans for high/medium findings within 10 business days of report delivery and target remediation timelines (30 days for medium, 90 for low/longer term items).

5) Evidence rotation: Add appendix language that describes a tiered sampling model (A controls quarterly, B controls semi-annual, C controls annual) with a named evidence owner and retention requirements.

I attached my draft redlines (MSA_redlines_karthik_20260813.docx). If MedicoHealth is comfortable with these caps and timelines we can update the security exhibit and produce a final PDF for DocuSign.

-Karthik
Associate General Counsel — Redwood Inference
(attachment: MSA_redlines_karthik_20260813.docx)
